profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. On its own site it describes its mission as raising awareness about the impacts of AI, equipping advocates with empirical research, building the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanizing researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. It says AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment people receive, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation, and that such systems can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination. The organization describes itself as building a movement to shift the AI ecosystem toward what it calls equitable and accountable AI.

Its site highlights two activities in particular. It urges people to opt out of facial recognition technology that the TSA is expanding in airports, and asks visitors to share their experiences with airport face scans as part of holding government agencies accountable for their use of AI. It also points to the Coded Bias film, which it says shows how the organization began, features people affected by harmful technology and women raising alarms about threats AI poses to civil rights, and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020. The site asks for monthly sustainers to support its work.

The record holds no products, no lawsuits, and no MCP servers for the organization. Its recorded law exposure is in Massachusetts, with a count of 120.
